problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=3{t}^{2}-8t+3,$ where $t>0$ is the time in seconds.  The positive direction is left to right. If the particle has velocity $v=0\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s},$ determine the time intervals in which the particle moves to the left.

activity_context.topic_title: Determining Characteristics of Moving Objects Using Integration

feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=2t-4,$ where $t>0$ is the time in seconds.  The positive direction is left to right. If the particle has velocity $v=12\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=6\,\text{s},$ determine the time intervals in which the particle moves to the left.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2t-4)\text{d}t \\  & ={t}^{2}-4t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(6)=12.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}12 & =(6)^{2}-4(6)+C \\ 12 & =12+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)={t}^{2}-4t.$

To find the time interval in which the particle is moving to the *left*, we must solve the inequality $v<0.$ This gives

$$
{t}^{2}-4t=t(t-4)<0.
$$

Plotting the graph of $v(t)$, we get the following picture.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14094087/assets/4ceab0aa50ce1a1fa8a49755ccc4f33a159cf5081be7ed86fe78d1453e2b5298.png)

From the graph, we see that $v<0$ whenever $0<t<4.$
